newsitem.title: CHINA: China to allow firms to issue convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: China to allow firms to issue convertible bonds.

text.p: China will shortly allow selected state firms to issue four billion yuan worth of convertible bonds as part of efforts to push forward reform of the state sector, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.
The newspaper said Beijing would select some of China's 500 biggest state enterprises to be part of the convertible bond experiment.
Listed firms will not be included in the experiment for the time being, it said.
China's has previously allowed a handful of listed firms to issue convertible bonds.
The State Council, the cabinet, has empowered the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the top securities watchdog, to be in charge of the new issue, the newspaper said.
Local authorities can recommend firms to participate in the experiment with the deadline for recommendations set at May 10, but the newspaper did not say when issue of the bonds would start.
"The issue of convertible bonds by key state enterprises will help them to open new channels for raising money," the newspaper quoted a CSRC spokesman as saying.

The spokesman said convertible bonds were a new financial tool in China. He called on local governments, exchanges and the companies involved to maintain strict supervision of the bond issue and said investors should be informed of the risks.
The bonds, if converted, would become shares in the issuing state firms, and could be listed on the stock exchanges with the approval of the securities authorities, the newspaper said.
The newspaper did not indicate whether any of the issues would be foreign currency denominated and therefore open to foreign investors.
